messages:
Sasha: paging — we are seeing sustained queue growth on gpu-pool-inference-eu-west, throttle increasing, lots of 429s in prod. Logs show pool at 100% and autoscaler hitting max_replicas. @Liam you oncall?

incident-bot: Incident created (INC-2026-2201). Severity: P1. Affected service: inference-runtime. Pager sent to oncall.

Liam: on it. I'm looking at metrics — qps up x3 vs baseline. Autoscaler logs: "scale attempt blocked: global_max_replicas_reached". Also continuous-batching healthy hits dropped; prefix-cache miss rate spiked to 82% 10m ago.

Priya: Confirming, rolling window shows a recent config rollout 2201233200 changed continuous_batching.max_delay from 5ms -> 50ms and prefix_cache.ttl from 1h -> 10s. That rollout completed ~18:06 UTC.

Kai: that explains increased per-request latency plus cache misses. Bigger batching delay increases head-of-line blocking and reduces throughput for short queries.

Liam: Mitigation plan: 1) revert batching max_delay to 5ms (eng-runtime runbook step) 2) temporarily bump gpu-pool autoscaler max_replicas + allocate extra reserved nodes 3) throttle non-critical background jobs. I'm starting revert now.

Sasha: do we need to page infra to spin more nodes? @Marta please standby.

Marta: infra paged, requesting +4 g4dn nodes in eu-west. ETA ~4m.

eng-runtime-bot: Triggering rollout revert for config set "batching-config" -> rolling back to v15. Command: /rollout revert batching-config v15

Liam: running revert... logs:
```
rollout: revert requested by Liam
fetching config v15
applying...
success: batching.max_delay=5ms, prefix_cache.ttl=3600s
```

Priya: Reverted. Observability: prefix_cache miss rate down to 18% within 60s, throughput improving.

Kai: Nice. However autoscaler still at cap, queue still elevated. Need short-term capacity bump.

Marta: infra: additional nodes provisioned and attached. New pool size +4 at 18:27 UTC.

Liam: Autoscaler now scales up to new nodes, pool freed up, queue draining. Throttle events decreased from 1200/min -> 120/min.

Sasha: Customer impact? CS reports increased latency in small chat customers and 5% request error rate for 18:06–18:28.

Customer Success: we've flagged top 12 customers on EU cluster, no data loss, only higher latency/errors. We sent outage note to account owners.

Kai: Root cause: rollout changed two parameters—continuous_batching.max_delay and prefix_cache.ttl — their combination increased batch wait and invalidated prefixes, causing more unique KV states and misses, higher per-token compute, saturating GPUs and hitting autoscaler limits.

Liam: Postmortem actions: 1) Add gating in rollout system to detect prefix_cache.ttl reductions beyond 10% without canary. 2) Add autoscaler elastic headroom for rapid regresses. 3) Add smoke test to CI simulating short-chat traffic to catch throughput regressions. 4) Run trace to validate KV cache hit rate per model.

Priya: I'll file the follow-up tasks. Assigning to eng-runtime and infra.

Sasha: good. Oncall handoff — Liam staying until queue < 5k and throttles < 1/min. Marta will monitor infra. Priya will own postmortem.

eng-runtime-bot: Incident INC-2026-2201 updated: status => mitigating. Next update in 30m or earlier on resolution.

Liam: current metrics: queue depth 1.2k -> trending down, p99 latency from 860ms -> 420ms, 429 rate down to 0.3%.

Sasha: thanks everyone. We'll run the postmortem template and include timeline. Closing updates once all followups triaged.

Customer Success: we'll follow up with customers tomorrow with RCA & timeline for safeguards.

Marta: infra note: AWS spot reclaim didn't play a role, nodes were on-demand.

Sasha: end."
